Description: Iraq invades Kuwait leading to severe Middle East crude oil supply disruption and price spike.
Financial crisis originating in East Asia leads to reduced global oil demand and sharp price decline.
Terrorist attacks in the US prompt global aviation downturn and temporary oil demand contraction.
US-led coalition invades Iraq causing Middle East geopolitical tension and oil supply uncertainty.
Lehman Brothers bankruptcy triggers global recession and severe crude oil price collapse from peak.
Conflict in Libya halts high-quality light sweet crude production, causing global price surge.
OPEC declines to cut production to preserve market share against US shale, initiating 2014-2016 price crash.
Lifting of Western sanctions on Iran allows Iranian crude exports to re-enter global market.
OPEC and non-OPEC producers (OPEC+) sign landmark agreement to curtail oil output and stabilize prices.
US withdraws from Iran nuclear deal and re-imposes oil export sanctions on Iran.
Drone strikes on Saudi Aramco processing plants briefly knock out ~5% of global oil production.
WHO declares global pandemic causing unprecedented global travel lockdowns and oil demand crash.
Price war between Saudi Arabia and Russia leads to massive supply glut and temporary negative WTI futures.
Full-scale invasion triggers major Western energy sanctions on Russia and surge in global Brent prices.
